messages.subject: Re: Four way cross and X-chromosome
parts:
I think you'll need to use the pattern of genotypes in the offspring to determine whether a marker locus is pseudoautosomal or "normal" X linked. That is, at a given marker, are the males all hemizygous (look like homozygotes, but with the one allele coming from their mother)? I'd call that a "normal" X marker, and would change the male genotype to from say homozygous A to AD, where D would be a placeholder for the Y chromosome.

karl

> Quoting Karl Broman <kbr...@biostat.wisc.edu>:

>>
>> Remind me: don't sticklebacks have a sex _locus_ rather than a pair of sex chromosomes?
>>
>> In this case, the rest of LG 12 would act like the pseudoautosomal region in mammals. And you'd want to just code the loci like the autosomes, and just be sure to include sex as a covariate in the mapping of any trait.
>>
>> karl
>>
